queries.hook: A fire lit by seeing what others achieved; the resolve to rise, gather your strength and take on what is yours to do.
queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the prize or looks sideways at others; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.
queries.story: A story of someone who set out to build or win something that was theirs to do, met the first test, and kept going.

hook.speaker: Chirakari
hook.setting: Ordered to kill his mother, Chirakari slowly weighs what a mother is.
hook.sanskrit: नास्ति मातृसमा च्छाया नास्ति मातृसमा गतिः / नास्ति मातृसमं त्राणं नास्ति मातृसमा प्रिया
hook.line: There is no shelter like a mother, no refuge like her, and no one as dear.
hook.translation: There is no shade like a mother, no refuge like a mother, no protection like a mother, no one as dear as a mother.
hook.why: In anger, and when loved ones seem to have wronged you, slow down.

prasang.title: Chirakari, the one who acts slowly
prasang.summary: In a jealous rage, the sage Gautama orders his son Chirakari to kill his mother and storms off. Chirakari, famous for slowness, weighs a father's word against a mother's worth for so long that Gautama returns, regretful, and finds them both alive.
prasang.story_hook: Ordered by his furious father to kill his mother, Chirakari did what he always did: he thought about it.
prasang.lesson: In anger, and when loved ones seem to have wronged you, slow down.

alternates.speaker: Bhishma
alternates.setting: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma how an eldest brother should treat his younger brothers, and they him.
alternates.sanskrit: दशाचार्यानुपाध्याय उपाध्यायान्पिता दश / दश चैव पितॄन्माता सर्वां वा पृथिवीमपि / गौरवेणाभिभवति नास्ति मातृसमो गुरुः
alternates.line: There is no teacher like a mother.
alternates.translation: A teacher outweighs ten instructors, a father ten teachers, and a mother ten fathers, even the whole earth. There is no teacher equal to a mother.
alternates.why: Overlook small faults, correct gently, share fairly, and don't let outsiders divide you.

prasang.title: Bhishma on elder and younger siblings
prasang.summary: Yudhishthira asks how the eldest brother should treat the younger ones. Bhishma: overlook small faults and correct gently, beware outsiders who sow division, divide property equally, and honour the mother above all.
prasang.lesson: Overlook small faults, correct gently, share fairly, and don't let outsiders divide you.

alternates.speaker: Chirakari
alternates.setting: Ordered to kill his mother, Chirakari slowly weighs what a mother is.
alternates.sanskrit: पुत्रपौत्रोपपन्नोपि जननीं यः समाश्रितः / अपि वर्षशतस्यान्ते स द्विहायनवच्चरेत्
alternates.line: Whoever still has their mother to turn to is a little child, even at a hundred.
alternates.translation: Even with sons and grandsons around him, someone who still has his mother to turn to lives like a two-year-old, even at a hundred.
alternates.why: In anger, and when loved ones seem to have wronged you, slow down.

verse.for_you: The shade you are seeking is already there, steady and near. You do not have to build it from scratch. Let the resolve you feel now be enough to hold you today.
verse.try_today: Notice one small comfort that already shelters you today.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: आशा नाम नदी मनोरथजला तृष्णातरङ्गाकुला रागग्राहवती वितर्कविहगा धैर्यद्रुमध्वंसिनी । मोहावर्तसुदुस्तरातिगहना प्रोत्तुङ्गचिन्तातटी तस्याः पारगता विशुद्धमनसो नन्दन्ति योगीश्वराः ॥
verse.line: Hope is a river: its water is wishes, its waves are craving, and its high banks are worry.
verse.translation: There is a river called Hope. Its water is wishes, its waves are craving; passions are its crocodiles, doubts its birds; it uproots the trees of courage; its whirlpools of delusion are hard to cross and deep, and its banks of worry tower high. Only great yogis, pure in mind, who reach the far shore, rejoice.
verse.why: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of craving
prasang.summary: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.
prasang.lesson: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

verse.try_today: Notice when wishing turns into craving, and let the wish rest as a wish.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the bank of your own resolve, watching the river of hope flow past.

why: The river called Hope (Bhartrihari, Vairagya Shataka 10)
Shows worry as part of one river fed by wishing

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on worship for rewards and worship without desire.
verse.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते । तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥
verse.line: Turn to me with your whole heart, and I will carry what you lack and guard what you have.
verse.translation: To those who think of me alone and worship me, ever devoted, I bring what they lack and preserve what they have.
verse.why: Trust eases the worry of getting and keeping.
verse.misuse: Not 'God will pay the bills, so don't plan'. Trust eases worry; it doesn't replace effort or prudence.

prasang.title: Worship with and without desire, and their fruits
prasang.summary: Those who worship for heavenly rewards return when merit runs out; those who think of him alone are carried and protected.
prasang.lesson: Trust eases the worry of getting and keeping.

verse.for_you: You are turning toward what you hope for. The part that lacks is held, and what you have is watched over. Let that be enough for today.
verse.try_today: Notice what you lack today, and let it rest in the thought of what you are turning toward.

why: The child relies on the mother and stops worrying.
the worry of getting and keeping is carried by God for the one wholly turned to him

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha describes King Janaka after his awakening, still ruling his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: भविष्यं नानुसंधत्ते नातीतं चिन्तयत्यसौ । वर्तमाननिमेषं तु हसन्नेवानुवर्तते ॥
verse.line: Don't chase the future or brood on the past. Meet this moment with a smile.
verse.translation: He does not chase the future or brood on the past; he simply goes along with the present moment, smiling.
verse.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

prasang.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

verse.for_you: You want to keep the turning going, and that resolve is already here. Meet the day with a smile, and the path to Vrindavan will open in its own time.
verse.try_today: Smile at the present moment as it comes to you today.
verse.scene_line: You walk through your garden of duties, and the sages' song is the present moment itself.

why: Do not chase the future or brood on the past.
a picture of a mind not living ahead or behind

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: निश्चित्य यः प्रक्रमते नान्तर्वसति कर्मणः / अवन्ध्यकालो वश्यात्मा स वै पण्डित उच्यते
verse.line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
verse.translation: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

verse.for_you: Decide to begin your path, and move forward without pausing halfway. Let your resolve guide you through each step today.
verse.try_today: Notice when you decide, and begin the very next step without pause.

why: Reflect fully, then decide and begin.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: नैव राज्ञा दरः कार्यो जातु कस्यांचिदापदि / अथ चेदपि दीर्णः स्यान्नैव वर्तेत दीर्णवत्
verse.line: In a crisis, you may be shaken inside. Don't let fear make your decisions for you.
verse.translation: A leader should never show fear in any crisis. Even if shaken inside, he should not act like a shaken man.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
verse.misuse: This is about not acting from panic, not about hiding your feelings from everyone.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.for_you: You are building something you want to see bloom. The inner shaking does not get to steer the wheel today.

why: Courage and steadiness are the wheels of the chariot that wins; do not let fear decide.
Composure for those who depend on one

story.title: The boy who kept studying through the twelve-year drought
story.story_hook: Twelve years of drought made every scholar forget what he knew. Except one boy, who never stopped reciting.
story.summary: A drought lasts twelve years. The great sages scatter in every direction to find food, and in the struggle to survive they forget what they had learned. One young man, the son of the river Sarasvati, is about to leave too.
story.lesson: What is practised daily through the lean years is what survives them; knowledge, not age, makes the teacher.
story.teaser: Twelve years of drought made every scholar forget what he knew. Except one boy, who never stopped reciting.
